title: Affine slice at one finite-type point of a Cohen--Macaulay relation
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $V,R$ be $S$-schemes. An equivalence relation $(s,t):R\to V\times_SV$ [def-pc-fibre-product] means that for every $S$-scheme $T$ the map on sections is injective and identifies $R(T)$ with an equivalence relation on $V(T)$. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ is called Cohen--Macaulay here if it is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and every local ring of every scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], with depth [def-weil-pbc-depth] equal to Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Assume $s,t$ are Cohen--Macaulay and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $v\in V$ be a finite type point, meaning that $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(v)\to V$ is of finite type [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. There are an affine $S$-scheme $A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], a locally finitely presented morphism $g:A\to V$ and a point $a\in A$ with $g(a)=v$, such that $h_A=s\circ\operatorname{pr}_R:A\times_{g,V,t}R\to V$ is flat, locally of finite presentation and locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite].

source.place: Tag 04N0 (lemma-max-slice-quasi-finite), clauses (1)--(4), with Situation 04MY (situation-slice), specialized to an equivalence relation, whose stabilizer is the identity V. Only the local slice and its saturation map are asserted.

proof.text: The relation gives a groupoid on $V$: the identity is the unique arrow with endpoints $(v,v)$, inverse reverses endpoints, and composition takes the unique arrow with the composite endpoints. These operations are natural on test schemes; [lem-pc-yoneda] realizes them as scheme morphisms. All groupoid equations hold because arrows with fixed endpoints are unique. For the stabilizer $G=V\times_{\Delta,V\times_SV}R$, a $T$-point over $v_T$ is an arrow from $v_T$ to itself; the unique such arrow is its identity. Thus $G\to V$ and the unit into $G$ are inverse morphisms (the same test-scheme argument and Yoneda). Hence $G_v\simeq\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(v)$, which has one point and dimension zero [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

source.place: 04MY; specialization of 04N0 to equivalence relations, trivial stabilizer

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-cm-groupoid-maximal-slice] to this groupoid and $v$. Its hypotheses are precisely the Cohen--Macaulay and local finite presentation assumptions and the given finite type point. Obtain $g_0:B\to V$, $b\mapsto v$, with $B$ affine, $g_0$ locally finitely presented, and $h_0:B\times_{g_0,V,t}R\to V$ Cohen--Macaulay and locally finitely presented. At $x=(b,e(v))$ its fibre has local topological dimension $\dim G_v=0$. In particular $h_0$ is flat, by the Cohen--Macaulay definition in the cited statement.

Choose affine neighbourhoods $D=\operatorname{Spec}C$ of $x$ in the source of $h_0$ and $E=\operatorname{Spec}K$ of $v$ in $V$, with $h_0(D)\subseteq E$ and $K\to C$ finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. It is finite type. The fibre of $D\to E$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_K\kappa(v))$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. It is an open neighbourhood of $x$ in the fibre of $h_0$, so its dimension at $x$ is still zero: the neighbourhoods contained in this open are cofinal in all neighbourhoods of $x$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ring-quasifinite-zero-fibre-dimension] to $K\to C$ at the prime of $x$. It is quasi-finite there; the affine pair $(D,E)$ therefore witnesses that $h_0$ is quasi-finite at $x$ [pqf-def-quasifinite].

A finite presentation is in particular a finite list of algebra generators. Thus $s,t,g_0$ are locally of finite type. Apply [lem-sfb-groupoid-quasifinite-locus-descent] to $g_0$: there is an open $W\subseteq B$ with $p^{-1}(W)$ the quasi-finite locus of $h_0$, where $p:B\times_{g_0,V,t}R\to B$. Since $x=(b,e(v))$ lies in this locus, $b\in W$. The restricted saturation $h_W:W\times_{V,t}R\to V$ is locally quasi-finite on its entire source.

Choose a principal affine open $A=B_f$ with $b\in A\subseteq W$; principal opens form a basis of the spectrum topology [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $a$ be $b$ viewed in $A$ and put $g=g_0|_A$. The map $A\to B$ is locally finitely presented: if $B=\operatorname{Spec}C$, its ring is $C_f=C[z]/(fz-1)$. Thus $g$ is locally finitely presented by [lem-sbc-locally-finite-presentation-composition]. The fibre-product universal property identifies $A\times_{V,t}R$ with the open subscheme $p^{-1}(A)$ of $B\times_{V,t}R$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. The stalk maps of $h_A=h_0|_{p^{-1}(A)}$ equal those of $h_0$, so it is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Its local finite presentations persist on principal opens: adjoining $z$ and the single relation $fz-1$ to a finite presentation gives one for each such open [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Finally, [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-restriction-to-opens] applied to $h_W$ gives local quasi-finiteness of $h_A$. The affine scheme $A$ has the induced $S$-structure and $g(a)=v$.

lean.statement: theorem exists_cm_relation_point_slice {S : Scheme.{u}} {V R : Over S} (s t : R ⟶ V) (hinj : ∀ T : Over S, Function.Injective (fun r : T ⟶ R ↦ (r ≫ s, r ≫ t))) (hrel : ∀ T : Over S, Equivalence (fun a b : T ⟶ V ↦ ∃ r : T ⟶ R, r ≫ s = a ∧ r ≫ t = b)) [Flat s.left] [Flat t.left] (hcm_s : ∀ (v : V.left) (x : s.left.fiber v), IsNoetherianRing ((s.left.fiber v).presheaf.stalk x) ∧ (IsLocalRing.depth (R := (s.left.fiber v).presheaf.stalk x) ((s.left.fiber v).presheaf.stalk x) : WithBot ℕ∞) = ringKrullDim ((s.left.fiber v).presheaf.stalk x)) (hcm_t : ∀ (v : V.left) (x : t.left.fiber v), IsNoetherianRing ((t.left.fiber v).presheaf.stalk x) ∧ (IsLocalRing.depth (R := (t.left.fiber v).presheaf.stalk x) ((t.left.fiber v).presheaf.stalk x) : WithBot ℕ∞) = ringKrullDim ((t.left.fiber v).presheaf.stalk x)) [LocallyOfFinitePresentation s.left] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation t.left] (v : V.left) [LocallyOfFiniteType (V.left.fromSpecResidueField v)] [QuasiCompact (V.left.fromSpecResidueField v)] : ∃ (A : Over S) (g : A ⟶ V) (a : A.left), IsAffine A.left ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation g.left ∧ g.left a = v ∧ Flat (pullback.snd g.left t.left ≫ s.left) ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation (pullback.snd g.left t.left ≫ s.left) ∧ Scheme.Hom.IsLocallyQuasiFinite (pullback.snd g.left t.left ≫ s.left)
